specPoints.text: describe energy transfers involving energy stores: • energy stores: chemical, kinetic, gravitational, elastic, thermal, magnetic, electrostatic, nuclear • energy transfers: mechanically, electrically, by heating, by radiation (light and sound)

primer.text: Every energy argument in this course runs on one model: eight stores that hold energy and four pathways that move it. This note fixes the vocabulary — system, equilibrium, stores, pathways — so that later calculations always have somewhere precise to put the joules.

lessons.title: Systems and energy stores
lessons.opening: Physics borrows a bookkeeping idea to keep energy arguments tidy: define a system — an object or group of objects — and then only energy crossing its boundary matters. Inside the accounts, eight named stores hold the energy while anything changing moves it between them.
keyPoints: A system means an object or a group of objects chosen for study.
Defining the system narrows the physics to what is relevant for the situation being observed.
A system in equilibrium transfers nothing; any change to the system moves energy between stores.
There are eight energy stores: kinetic, gravitational, elastic, magnetic, electrostatic, chemical, nuclear and thermal.
Moving objects fill the kinetic store; lifted objects fill the gravitational store; hotter objects fill the thermal store.

low.restatement: A system is any object or group of objects; changes to it transfer energy between the eight named stores, and an unchanged system in equilibrium transfers nothing.
low.analogy: A ledger with eight named accounts: nothing is spent or created, money simply moves between accounts whenever something happens to the system.
low.examPointer: Learn the eight stores as a fixed list — classification questions expect the exact names, not paraphrases.

medium.restatement: The system boundary decides which energy transfers are counted: an apple on a table transfers energy only once the table is removed, and the accounting then runs from the gravitational store into the kinetic store as it falls.
medium.analogy: Choosing a fence around a farm: only animals crossing the fence are counted, and the fence you draw changes the whole story.
medium.examPointer: State the system explicitly in long answers: the same falling apple is a different story if the Earth is inside or outside the system.

check.stem: What is a system in physics?

options.text: an object or group of objects
options.explanation: This is the stated definition of a system.
A system can be one object or a whole group.
Sources are parts of systems; the definition is broader.
Machines are systems, but so are apples and tables.

check.stem: An apple sits on a table and the table is suddenly removed. As the apple falls, which store-to-store transfer happens?

options.explanation: The transfer runs the other way while falling.
Falling transfers energy from the gravitational store into the kinetic store.
Heating is not what drives the fall.
Nothing is stretched in this scenario.

check.stem: A stretched spring is released. Which store held the energy before release?

options.explanation: Gravity is not what stretched the spring.
Stretched, squashed or bent objects hold energy in the elastic store.
Nuclei are not involved in a spring.
Charges are not the mechanism in an ordinary spring.

check.stem: Which store does EVERY object have, simply because it has a temperature?

options.text: the kinetic store of motion through space
options.explanation: The store tied to temperature is the thermal store.
All objects have energy in their thermal store; hotter means more.
Only magnetic materials interacting magnetically fill that store.
Chemical energy belongs to reactions, not to temperature alone.

check.stem: Energy is released during a nuclear reaction in a power station. Which store is emptied?

options.explanation: The thermal store GAINS as the reaction’s energy arrives.
Atomic nuclei release energy from their nuclear store in nuclear reactions.
Electrostatic interactions are not the source here.
Nothing is stretched inside the reactor.

check.stem: State the eight energy stores named in the stores table.
check.modelAnswer: Kinetic, gravitational, elastic, magnetic, electrostatic, chemical, nuclear and thermal.

check.stem: A system sits in equilibrium and nothing changes. State what is transferred while it stays in equilibrium.
check.modelAnswer: Nothing changes, so no energy is transferred while the system remains in equilibrium.

check.stem: Explain why defining a system is a useful step before describing an energy transfer.
check.modelAnswer: Defining the system narrows the parameters to only what is relevant, fixes the boundary that energy crosses, and makes the accounting unambiguous: transfers inside the boundary move energy between stores, while transfers across it are gains or losses for the system.

check.stem: Classify the store being emptied and the store being filled: (a) a log burns in a fire, (b) a car speeds up along a road.
check.modelAnswer: (a) the log’s chemical store empties and the surroundings’ thermal store fills; (b) the car’s chemical store empties and its kinetic store fills.

lessons.title: Energy transfer pathways
lessons.opening: Stores hold energy; pathways move it. The model names exactly four: mechanical work, electrical work, heating and radiation (light and sound). Any everyday transfer you can describe — a kettle, a falling apple, sunlight on a wall — reduces to these four crossings between stores.
keyPoints: Energy is transferred between stores by four pathways: mechanically, electrically, by heating and by radiation.
Mechanical work involves a force acting through a distance.
Electrical work transfers energy through moving charge in a circuit.
Heating covers particle-to-particle transfer such as conduction, and radiation (light and sound) transfers energy without a material medium.

low.restatement: Four pathways carry energy between the eight stores: mechanical, electrical, heating, and radiation (light and sound); every device description is a pathway joining two stores.
low.analogy: Four roads between eight towns: the stores are the towns and every journey of energy takes one of the four roads.
low.examPointer: When a question says describe the transfer, name BOTH the stores and the pathway: store → pathway → store.

medium.restatement: The pathway table separates how the energy crosses the boundary: force-through-distance is mechanical, charge-in-a-circuit is electrical, particle collisions are heating, and waves leaving the object are radiation.
medium.analogy: Payment methods for the same money: cash, card, transfer and bitcoin all move the same pounds between the same accounts.
medium.examPointer: Light and sound both count as radiation pathways — exam answers often forget sound is included.

check.stem: How many energy transfer pathways does the model name?

options.explanation: Three processes (conduction, convection, radiation) belong to HEATING, not to the pathway list.
The pathways are mechanical, electrical, heating and radiation.
Eight is the number of stores.
Two is far too few for the model.

check.stem: A kettle boils water. Which pathway carries energy from the mains supply to the heating element?

options.explanation: No force acts through a distance to deliver the energy here.
The mains supply transfers energy electrically to the element.
Light and sound are not the mains delivery route.

options.text: by heating directly from the mains
options.explanation: Heating happens after the element warms, not across the supply link.

check.stem: Which pathway can transfer energy across empty space?

options.explanation: Mechanical work needs a force and contact.
Electrical work needs a circuit of charge flow.
Radiation (light and sound... light especially) needs no material medium.
Conduction needs particles to collide.

check.stem: A person pushes a box along the floor at constant speed. Energy reaches the box’s thermal store through which pathway?

options.explanation: No circuit is involved in pushing.

options.text: mechanical work, then heating by friction
options.explanation: The push is mechanical work; friction delivers it to the thermal store by heating.
Sound from the scrape is radiation, but it is not the main route.

options.text: by heating from the hand directly
options.explanation: The hand is not touching the box bottom where friction acts.

check.stem: Which description matches the heating pathway?

options.explanation: That is mechanical work.

options.text: energy transferred by particle collisions or because of a temperature difference
options.explanation: Heating is the particle-level pathway driven by temperature difference.
That is electrical work.
That is the radiation pathway.

check.stem: State the four energy transfer pathways.
check.modelAnswer: Mechanical, electrical, heating and radiation (light and sound).

check.stem: State the pathway involved when a torch lamp lights a wall, and the store being emptied in the battery.
check.modelAnswer: The lamp’s energy reaches the wall by radiation (light), and the battery’s chemical store is being emptied.

check.stem: Explain why sound belongs to the radiation pathway even though sound needs a medium to travel.
check.modelAnswer: The pathway names describe how energy leaves the source and crosses to where it is received: sound carries energy away from the vibrating source as a wave, without any bulk movement of the source itself, which is exactly the radiation behaviour — the medium’s particles pass the wave along, but no matter travels with it.

check.stem: Describe the full store-pathway-store chain for a falling apple that splashes into a puddle.
check.modelAnswer: The apple’s gravitational store empties mechanically into its kinetic store as it falls; at the splash, the kinetic store empties by heating (into the water and apple thermal stores) and by radiation (the splash’s sound).

glossary.definition: An object or group of objects chosen as the focus of an energy description.
The state of a system in which nothing changes, so no energy is transferred.
One of the eight named places energy can be held: kinetic, gravitational, elastic, magnetic, electrostatic, chemical, nuclear or thermal.
One of the four ways energy moves between stores: mechanically, electrically, by heating, by radiation.

figures.caption: Energy is transferred by heating from the hot coffee to the mug to the cold hands
